name: sigrok-cli
desc: Sigrok command-line interface to use logic analyzers and more
why: Command-line front end to sigrok for logic analyzers and many instruments; a wonderful door into decoding real signals from hardware.

brief.what_it_is: sigrok-cli is a command-line tool written in C that gives terminal access to sigrok's signal-acquisition and decoding features. The README says it uses both libsigrok and libsigrokdecode to provide basic sigrok functionality from the command line. The README frames sigrok as a cross-platform, free and open-source signal analysis suite for devices such as logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and multimeters. The brief could not confirm the exact inputs and outputs from the README, so the scout note's point about decoding real signals from hardware is the only description of the output side.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says sigrok-cli provides sigrok's basic functionality from the command line and that it is "useful for scripting purposes."
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals beyond saying sigrok-cli is written in C and uses libsigrok and libsigrokdecode for the underlying device and decoder work. It does not describe the command syntax or how captured data is output.

commands_seen.context: Clones the sigrok-cli source code when building from git (README build section).
Enters the cloned source directory before building.
Generates the configure script; the README says this is needed when building from git.
Configures the build against the installed dependencies.
Installs sigrok-cli after a successful build.

brief.install_notes: The README lists the requirements as gcc or clang, make, pkg-config >= 0.22, libglib >= 2.32.0, libsigrok >= 0.5.0, and libsigrokdecode >= 0.5.0. Git, autoconf >= 2.63, automake >= 1.11, and libtool are needed only when building from git. The README points to the sigrok wiki's Building page for OS-specific instructions. The brief did not check the Homebrew formula, so nothing is known about hardware, accounts, or first-run configuration beyond what the README says.
brief.standout: It is a scriptable command-line front end to sigrok, which covers many instrument types and not only logic analyzers. The README's stated reason for it is scripting, which suggests it fits automated capture and decoding pipelines.
brief.status: The README says sigrok-cli "is in a usable state and has had official tarball releases." The README gives no release date or last-commit date, so recency is unknown. The brief did not check the repository's commit history or the Homebrew formula.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://sigrok.org/ could not be reached (URLError), so the brief relies on the GitHub README instead. Building from source needs several libraries and a configure step, and the README sends OS-specific details to an external wiki. The program as a whole is licensed under GPLv3 or later. The README does not describe command syntax, supported hardware, or example usage, so the brief cannot say what the commands do beyond the build steps.
